hypotheses.root_cause: DDR uncorrectable ECC error following rising corrected-error rate: Clock-domain-crossing synchroniser glitch in the controller
hypotheses.rationale: Corrected ECC errors trending up, then a read-retry, then an uncorrectable error and memtest mismatch indicate a marginal DRAM timing/training edge, often aggravated by voltage droop under load. Evidence contains the tell-tale(s) 'cdc synchronizer glitch', 'cdc' for RC_DDR_CDC_GLITCH. 1 of 1 similar historical incidents (runs 000000) were resolved as RC_DDR_CDC_GLITCH.
recommended_actions: Review CDC constraints on the controller/PHY boundary
Reproduce at corner voltage/frequency to isolate the glitch
Re-run DDR write-leveling/read training and widen timing margins
Correlate UE timestamps with PMU droop / thermal events
